wordmark.purpose: Lowercase alforria in the band; the only lowercase Barlow.

display.purpose: ALL CLEAR reward state when the queue empties.

verdict.purpose: The verdict word on the stamp.

counter.purpose: Band waiting count; 22px on the collapsed rail.

headline.purpose: Settings section titles, keys sheet title, empty-queue headings.

pane-title.purpose: Pane heads and project group names.

control.purpose: Stamps, Send, New session, settings navigation.

label.purpose: Slip heads, tool names, tabs, segmented buttons, message labels, column band.

data.purpose: Code, diffs, terminal, command plates, tool targets.

data-small.purpose: Paths, branches, ages, costs, counts, kbd, status line.

state.purpose: Lamp state codes and state pills.

themes.light: :root[data-theme="light"]; frontmatter keys suffixed -light map to the same custom property under this selector; accent is shared.

shadows.name: cursor-frame
shadows.purpose: Keyboard cursor row frame (add inset ±1px 0 side edges on first/last cells). A rule, not lift.

shadows.name: active-column
shadows.purpose: Active focus column, current mobile tab, and the error toast's top line.

shadows.name: selection-ring
shadows.purpose: Selected palette result, active rail row, and the disabled primary stamp's outline.

shadows.name: effective-default
shadows.purpose: Settings segment a value falls back to when unset.

shadows.name: open-lamp
shadows.purpose: Collapsed-rail lamp whose session is open in a column.

motion.name: t-feedback
motion.purpose: Press feedback, chevrons, and the stamp register/stamp-in (--t-feedback).

motion.name: stamp-hold
motion.purpose: Verdict visible before the slip folds.

motion.name: slip-fold
motion.purpose: grid-template-rows 1fr to 0fr collapse of a stamped slip.

motion.name: slip-arrive
motion.purpose: New slip slides 12px down and fades in.

motion.name: counter-tick
motion.purpose: Waiting numeral changes, entering from above.

motion.name: counter-flash
motion.purpose: Counter inverts to ink once on new arrival.

motion.name: row-fresh
motion.purpose: Table now-cell text fades ink to ink-2 on change.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Running tool mark, streaming caret, terminal cursor.

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hover and selection fills are immediate.

motion.name: read-delay
motion.purpose: A verdict key acts only after the active slip has been on screen this long; auto-repeat never acts (views/queue/queue.tsx).

motion.name: arrival-boot-grace
motion.purpose: Slips present at load do not play the arrival slide.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All animation/transition durations collapse and run once; smooth scroll off. The verdict still holds 480ms; the fold is instant.

breakpoints.name: band-compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: New session and designation drop labels.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: queue-w 360px, server address and band-tab keys hidden.

breakpoints.name: medium
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: context column hidden, New session icon-only, focus columns min 380px.

breakpoints.name: keys-two-column
breakpoints.purpose: min-width: keys sheet groups flow into two columns.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: single pane, 48px band, 56px bottom tabs, card rows, 50px stamps, 40px touch targets, 16px inputs.

breakpoints.name: column-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: @container on a focus column: composer key hint hidden.

icons.style: 16px viewBox, 1.5 stroke, square caps, miter joins, no fill except solid blocks

columns.openBeside: shift-click or the row's open-beside control; terminals always open beside

terminalPalette.note: Program output colours, scoped to the terminal well. Red leans crimson and yellow straw so neither reads as orange.

syntax.engine: shiki (lazy), monochrome theme mapped to classes

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Operating Datasheet"**

The alforria website is a component datasheet: an orange identifier band, condensed caps, numbered specifications and square stamped controls on cool paper. The web client is that same datasheet put into service. It is dense and dark-first, read for hours, and its job is to clear a queue of waiting agents and scan a table of live ones. It keeps the website's materials and inverts their emphasis. On the website orange announces the product. Here orange is silent until an agent needs the human, and then it is the only orange on screen.

The surface is flat and ruled. A cool near-black ground carries slightly lifted plates, and 1px cool-gray rules divide every region, row and cell. Pale ink carries the text. Barlow Condensed caps name things (panes, columns, tools, verdicts, controls). System sans carries sentences. Mono carries only what is data or code: paths, commands, costs, ages, token counts and state codes. Density is set by a 32px row and a 16px gutter. Motion is a grammar of immediate fills plus one signature: the 150ms registration-offset stamp that marks a cleared slip.

This record is taken from the shipped SolidJS build in `web/src/`: tokens and components in `ui/app.css` (tokens on `:root`, light theme on `:root[data-theme="light"]`), `ui/markdown.css`, `ui/terminal.css`, the authored icon set in `ui/icons.tsx`, diff rendering in `ui/diff.tsx`, the views under `views/`, and the self-hosted fonts in `ui/fonts/`. The first record was taken from the prototype (`web/prototype/`); the build ported its tokens unchanged and extended the system with navigation, the session rail, markdown, the terminal, toasts and settings controls. Brand lineage: `~/repos/alforria-website/DESIGN.md`. Every color key in the frontmatter maps to a CSS custom property of the same name prefixed with `--`. Keys ending in `-light` are the same property's value under `[data-theme="light"]`, and `accent` is identical in both themes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, with a light theme that returns to the website's paper and ink.
Orange means "waiting on you" and nothing else, always with ink on top.
Square corners, 1px rules, and flat tonal plates. No drop shadows and no gradients.
Condensed caps for names, system sans for prose, and mono only for data and code.
Ink-filled controls: the primary action is an ink stamp, never an orange button.
One signature motion: the registration-offset stamp.
Nothing moves under the cursor: rows keep their order, and a verdict key never lands on an item the human has not seen.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange means "an agent is waiting on the human" and nothing else. If the waiting state goes away, the orange goes with it: after the last slip clears, the band counter returns to ink-3 on the ground. Primary actions, selection, focus, progress, errors and toasts never use orange.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Orange Rule
rules.body: Every orange fill carries `accent-ink`. Orange text on the ground uses `accent-text`, never `accent`.

rules.name: The Diff-Tint Rule
rules.body: Green and red exist only to describe added and deleted lines. They never mark status, success, failure or cost. The terminal is the one exception, because its colours belong to the program being run, not to the interface.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state pairs its colour with a shape and a word. Lamps differ by form: filled for waiting, filled with a pulsing ring for working, half-filled for retry, hollow for idle, and slashed for fault. They always sit next to a mono state code (WAITING, WORKING, RETRY, IDLE, FAULT). Where a row is too narrow for the code (the rail, phone cards), the "now" line carries the word.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Barlow names, sans explains, mono measures. A sentence is never set in mono. Question text, permission explanations, fault recovery copy and toasts use sans. A path, command, cost or count is never set in sans.

rules.name: The Caps-Only-Condensed Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed is always uppercase, with the single exception of the wordmark. Inline mono inside a caps label keeps its own case and drops the tracking.

rules.name: The Mid-Token Wrap Rule
rules.body: Code never breaks inside an identifier. When a diff line wraps inside a narrow slip, break opportunities are inserted only at token boundaries (after `::`, `.`, `(` and `,`, and around spaced operators). Continuation lines hang 2ch past the line's own indent. Wide views (the Changes view, code viewer and markdown code blocks) scroll horizontally and do not wrap unless the reader turns wrapping on.

rules.name: The Stable Order Rule
rules.body: Rows never move under the cursor. The table and the rail order sessions by creation, with subagents under their parent, and a state change never reorders them. Surfacing what waits is the queue's and the Waiting filter's job, not the row order's.

rules.name: The Replace-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Opening a session swaps it into the active column. Adding a column is always a deliberate act (shift-click, "open beside", or a terminal).

rules.name: The Flat Plate Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand forward, give it a tonal step or an ink rule, never a shadow. The only offset in the system is the stamp's registration line, and it is a 1px rule, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Read Delay Rule
rules.body: A verdict key acts only on a slip that has been on screen for 500ms, and never on keyboard auto-repeat. After a verdict the next slip slides in under the same finger, and a new arrival can replace the active slip; a held or quick second key press must not approve something the human has not read.

rules.name: The Ready-Fill Rule
rules.body: A primary control that cannot act yet is an outlined plate, never a dimmed ink slab. Ink fill means "this will do something now".

rules.name: The Confirm-to-Loosen Rule
rules.body: Any change that removes the human from the loop asks first, in place, in a sentence that names its scope. Any change that puts the human back in applies at once.

dos: Do reserve `accent` for things waiting on the human: the lit counter, the active and inline slip heads, the column band, the rail's waiting bar, the waiting lamp, the pending tool mark, waiting-row veils, and the mobile queue badge.
Do put `accent-ink` on every orange fill, and use `accent-text` for orange words on the ground.
Do make primary actions ink-filled with ground text. Selection and the current item are also ink fills.
Do show a primary that cannot act yet as an outlined `plate` (1px `rule-2` inset ring, ink-3 text), and fill it with ink when it can.
Do draw focus as a 2px ink outline inset by 2px (`outline-offset: -2px`).
Do set every name and control in uppercase Barlow Condensed (700, or 800 for the wordmark, counter, verdict and display). Set sentences in system sans, and data and code in mono.
Do separate everything with 1px rules (`rule`, `rule-soft` between rows, `rule-2` for control outlines). Head spec lists with a 1px ink rule.
Do pair every state colour with a lamp shape and a mono state code.
Do keep hover fills immediate, and spend motion only on the stamp grammar (150ms feedback, 200ms fold, 260ms arrival).
Do break code only at token boundaries, with a 2ch hanging indent in narrow views.
Do keep the 16px left gutter and 32px rows when adding panes or tables.
Do keep row order stable as sessions change state, and open sessions into the active column unless the human asks for another.
Do gate verdict keys behind the 500ms read delay and ignore auto-repeat.
Do ask in place before any setting loosens the human's control, and apply tightening at once.
Do give every view a hash route, and every control on a phone a 40px target and 16px text fields.
donts: Don't use orange for primary buttons, links, selection, focus, progress, errors, toasts, brand decoration or input carets.
Don't use green or red outside diff lines, diff counts and the terminal's program output. Success and failure are told with ink, shape and words.
Don't round corners. The only round form is the 9px status lamp.
Don't add drop shadows, blurs or gradients. Inset 1 to 2px box-shadow lines are rules, and are the only permitted `box-shadow`.
Don't set prose in mono or data in sans.
Don't set Barlow Condensed in lowercase or sentence case, except the `alforria` wordmark.
Don't wrap code mid-identifier, and don't let wide code views wrap unless the reader asks. They scroll.
Don't put kickers or eyebrow labels above titles. Pane heads and slip heads are functional labels that carry state, counts or keys.
Don't reorder rows to surface waiting sessions; that is the queue's job.
Don't report success in a toast. Show it in place.
